children: The Transportation Security Administration announced on Tuesday that it expects to screen approximately 17.6M air travelers nationwide between Tuesday and next Monday. Notably, the TSA projects it will screen more than 3M passengers at U.S. airports on Sunday, November 29, the busiest day of the Thanksgiving holiday period.
The record is from the Sunday after Thanksgiving last year, November 30, 2025. TSA announced at the time that it had screened about 3,133,924 individuals.

Of course, the main worry going into this Thanksgiving weekend is whether the air traffic system will hold up, because it recently failed on a large scale. On November 13, the FAA had a technical problem at about 3:30 p.m. ET and issued a nationwide ground stop. Afterward, the agency estimated that 18K flights were canceled and 28K delayed. The early investigation traced the excessive data flooding its systems to two likely sources: a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas. It is still unclear whether contractor error or faulty equipment caused the meltdown, and the FAA and its contractor L3Harris

are still looking for the root cause. There is also a weather wildcard this year, as forecasters warn winter storms are likely, with mountain snow possible and rain across much of the South, Southwest and East Coast.

title: Airlines are on watch amid the Thanksgiving traffic rush
